purpose: This medication is an antibiotic given through an IV (directly into your vein) to fight serious bacterial infections. It is commonly used to treat infections in your lungs, sinuses, skin, or abdomen. Doctors choose this medicine when a strong antibiotic is needed quickly.
how_it_works: Moxifloxacin works by attacking and disabling the machinery that bacteria need to copy their DNA. Without being able to reproduce, the bacteria stop spreading and eventually die off. Your immune system can then clear up the remaining infection more easily.
common_side_effects: Some people experience nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, or headache. You might also notice some redness or discomfort at the IV site where the medicine enters your vein. Most side effects are mild and go away once treatment is finished.
warnings: This antibiotic can rarely cause serious tendon problems, including tendon rupture, especially in older adults or people taking steroids. It may also affect your heart rhythm, so tell your doctor if you have any heart conditions. Stop the medication and contact your doctor right away if you experience tendon pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe diarrhea, or signs of an allergic reaction like rash or trouble breathing. Avoid using this medicine if you are pregnant unless your doctor says it is absolutely necessary.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 400 mg given once a day through an IV infusion over about 60 minutes. Your doctor will decide how many days of treatment you need based on the type of infection you have. Always complete the full course of antibiotics, even if you start feeling better.
